content: The test image shows corn leaves with mottled/mosaic coloration, yellowish-green patches, and some brownish streaking along the leaves. Top candidates: viral diseases (Maize_dwarf_mosaic_virus, Maize_streak_virus), Goss_wilt, or Common_rust.

**Analysis:**

Test image observations:
- Corn leaves showing irregular **mottled/mosaic pattern** — alternating light yellow-green and dark green patches
- Pattern runs lengthwise, parallel to leaf veins
- Some brownish streaking on certain leaves
- Leaves appear somewhat curled/wilted
- Multiple leaves affected; plant appears field-grown and mature

**Comparison with references:**

| Candidate | Match |
|---|---|
| **Maize_dwarf_mosaic_virus** | Strong — alternating light/dark green mosaic streaks parallel to veins, same irregular mottling |
| Maize_streak_virus | Weaker — requires more dramatic white/cream high-contrast streaks |
| Goss_wilt | Weaker — would show distinct water-soaked brown lesions with "freckles" (bacterial exudate) |
| Common_rust | No — would show discrete raised orange pustules, absent here |
| Corn_Stunt_Spiroplasma | No — shows severe purple/reddish coloration, dead tissue |
| Gray_leaf_spot | No — shows rectangular gray-tan discrete lesions |

The mottled green-yellow mosaic pattern running parallel to veins is the hallmark of MDMV, and the test image matches this reference closely.
